Task: Design de novo protein binders for the human TREM2 IgSF domain.
Target the V-type Ig-like extracellular domain of human TREM2 (PDB 5ELI, ~15 kDa, β-sandwich with CDR-like loops at the ligand-binding apex). Aim binders at the IgSF domain to stabilize TREM2 on the cell surface — mimic the VHB937 mechanism, NOT the stalk-binding AL002 mechanism that triggers internalization. The stalk region (res 133–172) is absent from 5ELI, so ignore it.
5ELI construct sequence (IgSF domain + C-terminal His-tag): TGHNTTVFQGVAGQSLQVSCPYDSMKHWGRRKAWCRQLGEKGPCQRVVSTHNLWLLSFLRRWNGSTAITDDTLGGTLTITLRNLQPHDAGLYQCQSLHGSEADTLRKVLVEVLADPLGTKHHHHHH

Hard constraints:
* Each sequence ≤ 250 amino acids
* Ranking metric is ipSAE; optimize for it
* Experimental validation is BLI binding affinity, so favor designs likely to fold and bind in vitro (sane pLDDT, low interface PAE, reasonable expression/solubility)

Note: I want a IPSAE atleast above an .88

11	## Tooling & environment
12	
13	### Fresh Lambda VM bring-up (bare Ubuntu 24.04, NOT Lambda Stack)
14	Lambda VMs have come up as **bare Ubuntu 24.04** with NO driver/Docker (SETUP.md's "pre-installed" claim is false). Install order, all noninteractive:
15	1. `sudo DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive NEEDRESTART_MODE=a apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-580-server nvidia-utils-580-server` (580 = stable, CUDA 12/13; avoids the debconf whiptail under non-tty).
16	2. `sudo modprobe nvidia nvidia_uvm nvidia_drm` — no reboot; DKMS builds against the running kernel (6.8.0-62). `nvidia-smi` may say "couldn't communicate" until modprobe fully loads — retry after.
17	3. `sudo apt-get install -y docker.io` + `sudo usermod -aG docker ubuntu`.
18	4. NVIDIA Container Toolkit from the upstream apt repo (gpgkey `nvidia.github.io/libnvidia-container/gpgkey`) → `sudo nvidia-ctk runtime configure --runtime=docker && sudo systemctl restart docker`.
19	5. Verify: `sudo docker run --rm --gpus all nvidia/cuda:12.4.1-base-ubuntu22.04 nvidia-smi`.
20	
21	**Docker-group footgun:** `usermod -aG docker` does NOT propagate into the shell/session that ran it. `proteinclaw`'s LocalRunner calls `docker` directly, so wrap every invocation: `sg docker -c 'bash -c "source .venv/bin/activate && proteinclaw ..."'`. A fresh SSH login picks up the group and doesn't need this.
22	
23	**Persistent FS:** wire the §2 symlinks (`~/.cache/{huggingface,rfdiffusion,proteinmpnn,openfold}` + `~/.proteinclaw` → `/lambda/nfs/<name>/...`) BEFORE any weight download. Mount name varies per account (seen: `Daanish2`, `Daanishfiles`). Comes back empty on a fresh VM → all weights + Docker images rebuild (~30–60 min cold).
24	
25	### 2026-06-06 bring-up: node v22 + driver 580.159.03 (CUDA 13.0) both work
26	Ran the full bare-Ubuntu §"Fresh Lambda VM bring-up" recipe on this box (A10, no driver/docker/uv at start). Two deviations from the pinned versions, both fine: **node was v22.22.3** (not the pinned 20.x) and **claude-agent-sdk works against it**; `nvidia-driver-580-server` came up as **580.159.03 reporting CUDA 13.0**, GPU passthrough into `nvidia/cuda:12.4.1-base` container OK, `doctor` all PASS (weights WARN = expected, lazy). No reboot needed (modprobe). Docker 29.1.3. This box has **no Lambda NFS** — `~/.cache/*` weight symlinks (§2) were NOT wired; weights will land on the local 1.3 TB disk.
27	
28	### GPU is an A10 (24 GB) reporting 22 GB — sits exactly on the floor
29	`lspci` shows `GA102GL [A10]`; `nvidia-smi` reports **23028 MiB**, and `total_gb = 23028 // 1024 = 22`. The global VRAM floor was lowered 24→22 (commit `b5e222d`, in `doctor.py` `GLOBAL_VRAM_FLOOR_GB` + RFD3/AF2 `tool.yaml`) for exactly this card, so doctor reads "22 GB ≥ 22 GB floor → PASS". **Do NOT lower floors further** — a lower floor doesn't add memory, it just removes the OOM guardrail (violates "fail loud"). AF2-multimer on large binder+target complexes (>~400 aa) is the tightest step on 22 GB; fix OOM with a smaller binder / fewer recycles, not a lower floor.
30	
31	### Pinned versions that matter
32	`nvidia-driver-580-server`, `docker.io` (24.04 default) + `nvidia-container-toolkit`, `python3.12`, `uv 0.11.16`, `node 20.x`, `@anthropic-ai/claude-code`, `claude-agent-sdk 0.2.87`. Per-model image pins are in the Tool-wrapper section below.

36	## Tool wrappers (4-file convention + `_normalize.py`)
37	
38	### Shared LocalRunner mechanics (apply to every GPU tool)
39	- **Container UID/GID:** `docker run -u $(id -u):$(id -g)` so workspace artifacts aren't root-owned. Tool Dockerfiles must NOT set a restrictive `USER` (would block reading the bind-mounted entrypoint).
40	- **Weight caches mount at `/cache/<name>`** (not `/root/.cache`, which UID 1000 can't write). Each tool's Dockerfile sets its env (`HF_HOME=/cache/huggingface`, etc.) + `mkdir -p /cache/<name>`.
41	- **Build context staging:** `_ensure_image` copies the tool dir + `_SHARED_BUILD_FILES` (`_gpu_metrics.py`) into a tempdir so Dockerfiles can `COPY _gpu_metrics.py` (no path-traversal in build context). Add new shared helpers there.
42	- **Path translation:** `_translate_workspace_paths` rewrites `/workspace/...` in result envelopes → host paths. Containers tagged `--label proteinclaw.session=<sid>` (used by `proteinclaw cancel`).
43	- **`_normalize.py` per tool** (the allowed 5th file): parameter/PDB normalisation extracted so host-side tests import it without container-only imports. Tests MUST load it via `importlib.util.spec_from_file_location` under a **unique** module name — plain `from _normalize import` collides across tools in one pytest session.
44	
45	### Conditional JSON-Schema (`allOf`/`if`/`then`/`else`) in a tool.yaml silently DROPS the tool from the agent (2026-06-07)
46	**Symptom:** run `b269b01802e5` made **0 RFD3 calls** and the agent's plan.md said *"RFdiffusion3 … was not loaded in this session's deferred-tools list"* — it reused prior backbones instead. The immediately-prior run `a89c4dfe5a89` (before the edit) called RFD3 fine. **Root cause:** I had added an `allOf: [{if/then/else}]` block to RFD3's `tool.yaml` to make `required` conditional (de-novo vs partial mode). The registry's `Draft202012Validator.check_schema` *accepts* it, and `build_mcp_server` builds fine — but the agent runs under the **`claude_code` system-prompt preset** (`core._build_options`), which uses **deferred tools / ToolSearch** and sends each tool's schema as an **Anthropic tool `input_schema`**. The API tool-schema validator does **NOT** support `allOf`/`if`/`then`/`else`/`oneOf`/`anyOf` — so RFD3's schema was rejected and the tool silently vanished from the agent's loadable set (every other tool has a flat schema and survived). **Fix:** reverted RFD3 to a flat schema (no `required`, no `allOf`); the two modes are enforced at runtime by `normalize_args`/`normalize_partial_args`, NOT jsonschema (runtime args are never jsonschema-validated — confirmed: `router.route`→`runner.run` does no schema validation). **Rule: keep every `tool.yaml` `parameters` schema FLAT** — type/properties/required/enum/min/max/pattern only; no conditional keywords, or the tool disappears from the agent under the claude_code preset. tool.yaml is host-read by the registry (NOT baked into the image) so schema fixes need no rebuild.
47	
48	### RFD3 partial diffusion: `partial_t` is Angstroms, NOT timesteps (2026-06-07, GPU-verified)
49	RFD3 **does** support partial diffusion, but the param is `partial_t` = **Angstroms of noise** (RFD3 caps ≤15; field in `rfd3/inference/input_parsing.py`), NOT the classic RFdiffusion `partial_T` timestep count. The old skill refs to `partial_T=20`/`T=50` were wrong on both name-semantics and value (would've been a near-cold-start, and the wrapper never exposed any such param so the call would 404). Now wired into the wrapper: new params `start_pdb` (a prior binder+target complex under /workspace) + `partial_t` + `binder_chain`/`target_chain`; switches `run()` to `normalize_partial_args` + a contig-free `build_input_spec` branch (`{dialect:2, input:start_pdb, partial_t, is_non_loopy}` — RFD3 forbids `length`/contig with partial_t and re-noises the WHOLE complex "without constraints", target included). tool.yaml uses `allOf/if-then-else` to require `start_pdb` when `partial_t` present, else `target_pdb`+`hotspot_residues` (Draft202012 supports it; note: **call-args are NOT jsonschema-validated at runtime** — only `normalize_*` + RFD3 `prevalidate_inputs` enforce; schema is planner-facing). **Footgun: the image bakes `_normalize.py`/`implementation.py` via `COPY`, and `_ensure_image` only builds when the image is MISSING — so after editing wrapper code you MUST manually rebuild** (`docker build -t proteinclaw/rfdiffusion3:0.1.0 <staged ctx with _gpu_metrics.py>`), or delete the image. GPU-verified on run-29d's rank-1 complex (`partial_t=5`): 2 backbones, binder A=96/target B=112 preserved, first CA shifted ~0.6 Å (genuine local refinement). 28 normalize tests + skills check green. Skill now PREFERS partial diffusion as the first round-2 refinement (2-6 Å polish, 8-12 Å explore).
50	
51	### Per-model dep pins (load-bearing — don't modernize)
52	- **ProteinMPNN:** torch 2.4.1 cu121 on CUDA 12.4 base; bundled vanilla weights. `fix_positions` NOT implemented. Literature default for de-novo binders is `soluble_mpnn` (not yet wrapped — add `use_soluble_model`).
53	- **ESMFold:** `facebook/esmfold_v1` via HF transformers; **torch==2.6.0** cu124 required (CVE-2025-32434 — older torch refuses `from_pretrained`). ~14.2 GB VRAM. >1024 aa rejected at normalize.
54	- **RFD3:** `rc-foundry[rfd3]` on base `rosettacommons/foundry:slim`; `HOME=/tmp`+`XDG_CACHE_HOME=/tmp/.cache`. Checkpoint via `foundry install rfd3` → `~/.cache/rfdiffusion`. Canonical ckpt URL `files.ipd.uw.edu/pub/rfd3/rfd3_foundry_2025_12_01_remapped.ckpt`. **Patch `/app/foundry/.env`** (sed) to prepend `/cache/rfdiffusion` to `FOUNDRY_CHECKPOINT_DIRS` — dotenv loads at runtime and overrides a plain `ENV`. Outputs `.cif.gz` (atom14 mmCIF) → wrapper auto-converts to PDB via biotite. Hotspots are per-atom (`{A56:"CB,CG"}`); wrapper defaults each residue to `CA,CB` (Gly→`CA`).
55	- **AF2-multimer (ColabFold):** base `nvcr.io/nvidia/cuda:12.2.2-cudnn8-...` — **MUST be cuDNN 8** (CUDA 12.4 ships cuDNN 9 → jax rejects). `colabfold[alphafold]==1.5.5`, `jax[cuda12]==0.4.23` (0.4.24+ removed `jax.linear_util`), `numpy<2`, `MPLCONFIGDIR=/tmp/matplotlib`. OpenFold params (~5 GB) lazy-download on first call. `complex_confidence` = mean binder-chain CA pLDDT = the ranking signal.
56	
57	### ipSAE interface metrics in the AF2 envelope
58	Dunbrack's `ipsae.py` (MIT, numpy-only) fetched into the image at build, **pinned to SHA `6174cf9e71cb1bd660cc805856a18c4871a6dec3`** (`IPSAE_SHA` ARG). `_compute_ipsae` derives `ipsae/iptm/pdockq/pdockq2/lis` from the rank-1 PAE matrix (`*_scores_rank_001_*.json`). ipSAE is **derived, not a ColabFold field**; output txt cutoffs are zero-padded 2-char (`5`→`05`); ipSAE is asymmetric (surface the `Type==max` row). **Soft-fail by design:** scorer failure → structure still returns, `ipsae=null` + `ipsae_error`. Ranking still sorts by `complex_confidence`; ipSAE/iptm are advisory (`ipsae ≳ 0.3` plausible). DB schema v1→v2 added `ipsae/iptm/pdockq/lis`. **STILL OPEN:** the AF2 image's `RUN wget` ipSAE layer is unverified in-container on GPU here — rebuild `proteinclaw/af2multimer:0.1.0` + one AF2 call before trusting it.

62	## Plain-Python tools (data + research)
63	
64	Shared layer: `tools/_http.py` (UA + timeouts) and `tools/_paths.py` (session workspace + per-host cache) — reuse, don't roll your own `requests`. Note: PRD §9.1's `web.py` (DuckDuckGo) was **never built** — general web search is the SDK's built-in WebFetch/WebSearch.
65	
66	- **UniProt:** `recommendedName.fullName.value` is the formal name (e.g. "Programmed cell death 1 ligand 1"), NOT the alias ("PD-L1"). Aliases under `alternativeNames` are not extracted in v1 — footgun for exact-match callers.
67	- **PDB:** `_filter_pdb` matches TER records by their own chain id (col 22), not a trailing-state flag — otherwise a discarded chain's TER leaks and naive parsers (PyMOL/Biopython) mis-read residue ranges.
68	- **`data.pdb_fetch` counts ordered waters/HETATM as chain residues.** 1UBQ chain A reports "134 residues, no gaps" but only 1-76 are protein; 77-134 are waters. `gaps: []` does NOT mean the whole range is protein — verify the true protein span (last `^ATOM` residue) before cropping. (This is the lesson the agent itself recorded in `skills/learned/target-resolution.md`.)
69	- **Literature/PubMed rate-limits:** a 429 → `{rate_limited: true, results: []}` is correct degradation (PRD §10.2), NOT a tool bug. `research.{literature_search,pubmed_search}` are single-query (NCBI throttled the old parallel path).
70	- **RCSB Search API:** response key is `result_set` (underscore); per-entry metadata (resolution/date/method) needs a 2nd Data-API pass (`data.rcsb.org/rest/v1/core/entry/{id}`).

74	## Agent core & skill file
75	
76	### Auth: OAuth via `claude login`, NOT `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` (the trap)
77	The Agent SDK reads OAuth from `~/.claude/.credentials.json` → subscription billing automatically. **If `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is set it silently wins**, billing pay-as-you-go while you think you're on subscription. `doctor.check_claude_auth` is 4-state (OAuth=PASS, OAuth+key=WARN-trap, key-only=PASS-api, neither=FAIL). `~/.proteinclaw/config.toml` holds model selection only — no secrets. Unset the key + `sed -i '/ANTHROPIC_API_KEY/d' ~/.bashrc`.
78	
79	### Research fan-out + the scout-refusal finding (hard-won, A/B-verified)
80	Scouts are read-only `research` (Sonnet) / `research_pro` (Opus escalation) subagents in `core.py:_research_agents()`. **The runtime spawn tool is `"Agent"`, NOT `"Task"`** — `_build_options` allows both; under `bypassPermissions` the `allowed_tools` list is documentation, not enforcement (verify tool names from a real trace). Key finding: Sonnet's safety classifier **refuses immune-checkpoint interface/residue queries at the TOPIC level — rephrasing/context does NOT help** (2×2 A/B: sonnet+PD-L1-residues REFUSED, opus+same OK, both fine on benign targets). Opus only helps with pure-retrieval framing (no design-intent line, no drug brand names). **Robust fix = ROUTING, not fighting the filter:** determine hotspots via the main agent's own `Bash` structural sandbox (contact/BSA on the co-crystal PDB) — reliable, zero refusals, more accurate; point scouts only at filter-safe topics (prior campaigns, fold designability, length/topology, developability). The propose→challenge(DEFEND)→adjudicate→converge debate mechanic is **verified firing** (e.g. TREM2 run `6e8c60a78622`: 6 scouts incl. 2 DEFEND, the agent overturned an epitope hypothesis on cited evidence). A dedicated `analysis.interface_residues` MCP tool (hotspots never touch an LLM) is the clean long-term fix.
81	
82	### Agent stops early + mis-narrates round count (2026-06-06)
83	Two related findings on the TREM2 runs. (1) **The agent narrated "stopped at round 2 of 4" on runs that were launched with `--rounds 1`** (`run_started.rounds==1` is authoritative; both `adbe5874aeb4` and `29d98715cdb4` were rounds=1). With rounds=1 the budget addendum says "1 round, run pipeline once" — the agent did an internal broad-then-focused MPNN re-sample within the single round and invented the "/4" frame. Lesson: trust `run_started.rounds` in the trace, not the agent's prose, for the actual cap. (2) **Even when told to iterate, the agent bailed early** citing "diminishing returns / same geometric constraint / no new hypothesis." Tightened both `_rounds_addendum` (capped multi-round branch in `core.py`) and `skills/proteindesign.md` §Self-refining loop with a **hard "do NOT stop early while gate unmet and budget remains" rule** + a structurally-distinct-pivot ladder (new topology/epitope/length regime) so "no new idea" → *generate one*, never finalize. Early finalize is now permitted ONLY when the gate is met (≥3 hits). `test_rounds.py` (8) + `skills check` (27) green. Note: the ipSAE 0.93 gate is unreachable (best observed 0.82), so with this change a capped run will now spend its full budget every time — intended, per owner.
84	
85	### `run_started` trace ALWAYS logged rounds=1 — logging bug, now fixed (2026-06-07)
86	`TraceWriter.run_started` has `rounds: int = 1` default and `core.py` called it WITHOUT passing rounds (`_drive` never even received it) → **every** run's `run_started` event logged `"rounds": 1` regardless of the real `--rounds` flag. This silently misled diagnosis (I repeatedly concluded "you passed --rounds 1" from the trace when the user had passed 4). The real cap lives only in the `_rounds_addendum` text the agent sees + `effective_max_turns`. Fixed: threaded `rounds` through `run_campaign`→`_drive`→`run_started`. **To know a run's actual round budget, do NOT trust pre-fix traces' `rounds` field** — infer from RFD3 call count / plan.md round narration instead. (Run `5707e91b52df` logged rounds=1 but genuinely ran 4 rounds incl. 2 partial-diffusion refinements.)
87	
88	### Confirmation pass (num_models=5) is a ROBUSTNESS test, not a score-lifter (2026-06-07)
89	Empirical from run `5707e91b52df` round 4: re-scoring top-6 at num_models=5/num_recycle=8 left ipSAE ≈ unchanged or slightly LOWER for 5/6 solid designs (delta -0.02..0.0), and **collapsed** the 6th (triage 0.828 → confirmed 0.635 — a lucky single-model outlier). So the pass catches false positives; it does NOT lift a real design's ipSAE. The earlier skill claim "ensembled ipSAE is usually higher and tighter" was **wrong** and is corrected in `proteindesign.md` §Confirmation pass + `tools/alphafold2_multimer.md`. Practical: ship designs with a small triage→confirmed delta; drop collapsers. Also: **partial diffusion + RFD3 schema fix CONFIRMED working in a real agent run** here (RFD3 called 3×: 1 denovo + partial_t=3 + partial_t=2). Realistic ipSAE ceiling for unconditioned RFD3 on the TREM2 IgV apex is **~0.82** (3 runs: 0.75/0.821/0.817 confirmed) — ≥0.88 needs strand-conditioning / Rosetta relax / AF3, none wired.
90	
91	### Research/debate fan-out made MANDATORY per round (2026-06-07)
92	Observed: recent TREM2 runs (`b269b01802e5`, `a89c4dfe5a89`, `29d98715cdb4`) had **zero** research/debate/web events — the agent skipped the §1.5 fan-out + §1.7 debate entirely, citing "the learned IgV playbook already applies" in plan.md (and all were rounds=1, so no per-round re-research either). Per owner, made research+debate **mandatory every round**: new Cardinal rule + "(MANDATORY every round)" on §1.5/§1.7 headers + self-refining-loop step 3 now says a refinement round with no fresh fan-out+debate is a *skipped* round. Kept the content-filter routing intact (hotspot/residue questions → structural sandbox, not scouts; a refused sub-topic may be dropped after one `research_pro` escalation — but never a full skip). Note this is enforced only by skill text (the agent can still ignore it under bypassPermissions); the audit signal is plan.md + `subagent_spawn` trace events. skills check (27) green.
93	
94	### `freesasa` is NOT in the agent's venv
95	The agent's `Bash` scratch runs in the **host venv** (freesasa only lives in the GPU tool *containers*). So its structural sandbox uses **biopython's Shrake-Rupley + NeighborSearch**, not freesasa — the skill says so explicitly (the freesasa import is a benign error the agent degrades around).
96	
97	### Skills: lean core + progressive disclosure + self-evolution
98	- Core `skills/proteindesign.md` (~24k) is concatenated into the system prompt every run; per-tool detail lives in `skills/tools/<tool>.md`, **Read on demand**. `skills.py:load_skill_text()` appends a **Tool skill index of ABSOLUTE paths** (relative wouldn't resolve from the run-dir cwd) and also indexes optional `skills/learned/*.md`. Fails loud if core or `tools/` is missing/empty. Antibody design content removed (out of scope).
99	- **`plan.md`** is the agent's run notebook (notes/reasoning/scout-hypotheses/debate-log/converged-hypothesis), written by the agent (skill §1.7); the agent's cwd IS the run dir, so relative `plan.md` lands in `runs/<id>/`. `core.py` seeds an honest template ("if this seed survives, the agent never deliberated"). (Unified from the old `hypotheses.md`.)
100	- **Self-evolution (2026-05-26):** the agent may optionally, at a round boundary, append a durable lesson to a tool skill or create `skills/learned/<topic>.md`. `core.py` grants the skills dir via `add_dirs` (the SDK option — `cwd` is NOT a hard write-jail; the agent already Reads abs paths outside cwd). Edits are **append-only `## Learned (run <id>, <date>)` blocks** (NOTES-style) → preserves the content-lock invariant tests, so they're a loud safety net. Surfaced in run summary + `result.json`; review/revert via `proteinclaw skills {diff,log,reset,check}` (reset does `git checkout` + `git clean` to also remove untracked new skills). Source/editable-install only. **Live-validated** on 1UBQ run `45df3147af56`: agent wrote a new learned skill, no permission error.
101	- **Invariant-test footgun:** `test_skill_invariants.py` locks specific strings; after the tool-skill split, tool-detail tokens (`output_binder_chain`, `1024`, `confidence`, `msa_degraded`) live in the split files — use the `_all_skill_text()` helper (core + tool files) for those; core-only invariants check `load_skill_text()`.
102	
103	### `proteinclaw cancel` (schema v2→v3)
104	Stops real work, not just a DB flag: `docker kill` containers by the `proteinclaw.session` label + SIGTERM the recorded `runs.pid` (new column) + mark `cancelled`. Soft-fails (missing docker/dead pid). **Runs started before this landed aren't truly cancellable** (no pid, unlabelled containers).
105	
106	### Ctrl-C is graceful; SIGKILL/timeout is not
107	`_drive` catches `(KeyboardInterrupt, asyncio.CancelledError)` (BaseExceptions the old `except Exception` missed) → status `cancelled`, triage on partials (the triage block sits OUTSIDE the `with TraceWriter`). A background-task **timeout kills with SIGKILL/SIGTERM, bypassing this** → no in-process `result.json`, SQLite row stuck at `running`; re-run `parse_trace` by hand.

111	## Persistence & reporting
112	
113	- **report.html surfaces two reasoning views.** `_collect_reasoning` → prose (`assistant_text` only). `_collect_activity` (2026-05-26) → a STRUCTURED "Run activity" timeline: `subagent_spawn` (the debate scouts, incl. DEFEND "Challenge:" rounds), pipeline `tool_use` (RFD3/MPNN/ESM/AF2/interface_metrics with arg hints), and `Write`/`Edit` to `skills/` (self-evolution). Plus a "Skills evolved this run" block from `summary.skill_edits`. Both passed via `render_report(extra_meta=...)`. The raw `trace.jsonl` always had these events; the report just never rendered them as structure before.
114	- **Triage reads the (lossy) trace.** `triage.parse_trace` re-parses each tool envelope straight out of `trace.jsonl`, which `TraceWriter` byte-trims. A too-low cap silently corrupted the single fat ESMFold batch envelope (~18 KB for 48 designs) → `json.loads` failed → all `esm_monomer_plddt` None. Trim cap raised 4000 → **100_000**. Footgun: any tool returning a large list-of-dicts envelope must stay under the cap, or triage needs an untrimmed side-channel.

16	and don't engage the target. **Practical rule:** until the wrapper gains strand conditioning, spend

18	backbones as low-yield. A sparse 4-hotspot hint of the aromatic/hydrophobic anchors (Y56, M115,

22	## Learned (run adbe5874aeb4, 2026-06-06): on TREM2-like Ig-V apices, binders converge on the CDR2 hydrophobic edge and consistently miss the peripheral charged anchors (R47, R98)
23	Targeting TREM2 5ELI chain A crop 20-131 with 5 sparse hotspots A44/A47/A74/A76/A98 (W/R/F/R/R covering
24	CDR1+CDR2+CDR3), the IgV α-helical-bundle rule held: BB7 (α-bundle) produced the top 3 hits in both

70	The core skill's Confirmation-pass guidance ("ensembled is usually higher and tighter than single-model
71	triage") was tested directly on 6 top TREM2 candidates (5ELI crop 20-131, CDR2-ridge hotspots, helical
72	bundle topology). Result: 5 of 6 designs confirmed within delta ±0.02 of their single-model ipSAE (0.801,
73	0.806, 0.814, 0.817, 0.817 — vs triage 0.821, 0.806, 0.814, 0.804, 0.822); 1 of 6 collapsed (R2-8 triage
74	0.828 → confirmed 0.635, the single-model was a lucky-rank-1 outlier). NONE were lifted by ensembling.
75	**Why it generalizes (to TREM2 / Ig-V apices, single-helical-bundle, ipSAE ~0.8 regime):** when the
76	single-model ipSAE is already at the architecture's ceiling (~0.82 here per the prior learned blocks),

82	(d) **For Ig-V apex campaigns where the user demands ipSAE > 0.85: don't spend round-4 budget on

7	## Learned (run 45df3147af56, 2026-05-26): the reported chain residue count includes ordered waters/HETATM — crop to the protein range, not the chain length
8	On 1UBQ, `data.pdb_fetch` reported chain A as "134 residues, 1-134, contiguous, **no gaps**", and the
9	chain-inspection envelope likewise gave `residues_present_first_last: [1,134]`, `gaps: []`. But ubiquitin
10	is a 76-aa β-grasp domain — only residues 1-76 are protein (602 ATOM atoms; last ATOM = GLY A 76); residues
11	77-134 are 58 ordered crystallographic **waters** (HETATM) that the tool counts as chain residues. Cropping
12	naively to the reported `1-134` would feed 58 waters to RFD3 as "target residues."
13	**Fix / generalizes to any crystal structure with ordered solvent or ligands modeled in the protein chain:**
14	the gap inspector's clean `gaps: []` does NOT mean the whole range is protein. Before choosing a crop,
15	verify the true protein span — e.g. a one-line `Bash` check for the last `^ATOM` residue
16	(`grep '^ATOM' file.pdb | tail -1`) or compare ATOM vs HETATM counts — and crop to the folded domain
17	(here `A/1-76`), not to `residues_present_first_last`.

## CycleRFdiffusion for TREM2 Binder Design

TREM2 (Triggering receptor expressed on myeloid cells 2) plays a central role in regulating microglial function in the central nervous system and has emerged as a promising therapeutic target for Alzheimer's disease.

### The Design Pipeline

A cyclic peptide design pipeline integrates CycleRFdiffusion, ProteinMPNN for sequence design, and HighFold for structural prediction and screening. The CycleRFdiffusion model was engineered by modifying the RFdiffusion framework specifically for cyclic peptide backbone generation.

### Results and Validation

Using the TREM2 structure as input, researchers generated and screened 1,500 peptide–target complexes, prioritizing four candidates that met structural and energetic criteria. Subsequent biophysical evaluation identified TP4 as a TREM2 binder, demonstrating consistent binding in spectral shift, microscale thermophoresis, and surface plasmon resonance.

### Significance

The study introduces a generalizable computational pipeline for cyclic peptide discovery and establishes proof-of-concept that small, AI-generated peptides can modulate CNS immune checkpoints.

This research was published in 2025, with the full paper appearing in *Bioorganic & Medicinal Chemistry Letters* and as a preprint on bioRxiv in September 2025.

## De Novo TREM2 Binders with Helical Structures (2024-2026)

A study identified a binding model in which a helix-loop-helix motif within the ApoE3 hinge and C-terminal region forms a transient hydrophobic pocket that wraps around the hydrophobic tip of the TREM2 ectodomain. This model is further supported by de novo-designed mini-protein binders.

More specifically, the two top binders, BindCraft8 and Odesign2, exhibited high helical content, consistent with their designed folds. The research employed circular dichroism (CD) spectroscopy to investigate the structural basis and analyze the secondary structures of the 13 mini-proteins.

Additionally, a framework was applied to the design of cyclic peptide binders targeting TREM2, with TP4 emerging as a validated TREM2 binder, displaying consistent binding signals and yielding an equilibrium dissociation constant (Kd) in the sub-millimolar range.

The primary source is a preprint dated April 24, 2026 from bioRxiv titled "XL-MS and De Novo Protein Design Identified a Common Motif for TREM2 Binding," and another from September 2025 on "AI-Guided Design of Cyclic Peptide Binders Targeting TREM2."

I found the research article you're looking for. The search results include the paper published as PMC11419269, which discusses biophysical mapping of TREM2-ligand interactions.

Here's a summary of the key findings:

The researchers designed a panel of 28 different TREM2 variants for use in quantitative BLI binding assays to map TREM2 binding surfaces for various ligands. These mutations are mainly located in the previously identified binding surfaces in the hydrophobic site, basic site, and site 2.

**Ligand Binding Sites:**

ApoE and TDP-43 bound at or near a common hydrophobic site, while C1q and IL-34 engage unique surfaces mainly located on the basic site. More specifically:

- Mutations to the hydrophobic site ablated binding to apoE4 and TDP-43.
- Binding to C1q was disrupted most strongly by mutations to the basic site, including R46, with some mutations to the hydrophobic site also attenuating binding.
- TREM2 binding to IL-34 was mediated by the basic site at a surface centering on R76.

The results reveal an intriguing promiscuous binding surface on TREM2 and provide information to drive further functional and structural studies, as well as strategies for therapeutically targeting TREM2.

# Data Extraction from HER2 Minibinder Design Study

Based on the provided article, here is what I found for your requested parameters:

## (1) BLI Hit Rates / Experimental Validation Success

The study used **surface display technology** rather than BLI. Of 31 computationally designed minibinders, only **2 showed binding** (0_710_9 and 2_703_6), representing approximately **6.5% functional validation rate**. The authors note: "For the remaining designs, no detectable binding was observed; because surface-display levels were not quantified in this assay, we cannot exclude limited display as a contributing factor."

## (2) Sequence Composition Filters

**Not explicitly reported.** The study does not disclose specific filters for charge, hydrophobic fraction, tryptophan content, or sequence entropy thresholds.

## (3) AF2 Thresholds Applied

The researchers applied: **pAE_interaction < 10 and pLDDT > 70**. These screening criteria were "applied to two-chain complexes comprising a truncated HER2 domain IV and each designed minibinder," yielding 31 candidates meeting these thresholds.

## (4) Soluble E. coli Expression Rates

Of 31 designed minibinders, **25 constructs were successfully cloned** (81%), but the study does not specify soluble versus insoluble fractions for purified protein yields.

## (5) soluble_mpnn vs vanilla ProteinMPNN Comparison

**No comparison provided.** The study employed "ProteinMPNN(FastRelax)" but made no comparative analysis against alternative sequence design approaches.

The evidence is now sufficient to synthesize the hypothesis. Here is the consolidated picture:

---

HYPOTHESIS: De novo alpha-helical-bundle miniproteins of 60-100 residues, targeting the apical hydrophobic patch of the TREM2 IgV ectodomain (CDR1 residues 40-47, CDR2 residues 67-78, and the 115-120 loop of PDB 5ELI), represent the topology-length combination with the highest expected hit rate, because (a) a helix-loop-helix motif is the experimentally confirmed endogenous-binding architecture at the TREM2 hydrophobic tip and (b) RFdiffusion/BindCraft campaigns against analogous IgV-fold targets (PD-1, PD-L1, CTLA-4, BCMA, CD19, CD22) uniformly converge on 3-helix-bundle scaffolds of 60-120 residues as the predominant successful topology.

EVIDENCE:

- Crystal structures of the TREM2 IgV ectodomain (PDB 5ELI) reveal that the apical ligand-binding site is a positively charged cleft capped by a hydrophobic patch, with L69 and W70 identified as functional hotspot residues whose mutation abolishes ApoE4 binding; the hotspot clusters across CDR1 (residues 40-47), CDR2 (67-78), and loop 115-120. (PMID 33090700, PMC8026773)

- A 2026 bioRxiv study (Perera et al.) performing cross-linking mass spectrometry (XL-MS) combined with de novo protein design found that the top two validated TREM2 minibinders, BindCraft8 and Odesign2, both exhibited high helical content by circular dichroism and employed a helix-loop-helix motif that wraps the hydrophobic apical tip of TREM2; this is the only published direct de novo protein binder campaign against TREM2 with experimentally confirmed hits. (PMID 42079091, DOI 10.64898/2026.04.23.720433)

- A 2025 study (Shu et al.) using CycleRFdiffusion against TREM2 (PDB 5ELI chain B, binder lengths 30-75 residues) identified cyclic peptide TP4 as a validated binder via SPR and MST, using the same apical hydrophobic epitope; this confirms the apical patch as accessible to designed cyclic scaffolds but the sub-millimolar Kd reported suggests that compact alpha-helical miniproteins with larger burial area may outperform short cyclic peptides on this target. (DOI 10.1016/j.bmcl.2025.xxx; biorxiv 10.1101/2025.09.18.676322)

- Systematic biophysical mapping of TREM2 using 28-variant BLI assays (Bhatt et al. 2024, PMID 39315272, PMC11419269) confirmed a shared hydrophobic binding surface engaged by ApoE and TDP-43 (centered on L69/W70 at the apical hydrophobic patch) as functionally distinct from the adjacent basic site (centered on R46/R76); this surface map provides a rational hotspot specification for diffusion-based design.

- RFdiffusion/BindCraft campaigns against IgV-fold immune checkpoints (PD-1, PD-L1, CTLA-4) demonstrated de novo binder success at the 60-100 residue range, predominantly yielding 3-helix bundles that dock the flat GFCC' face of the IgV domain; the Baker lab proof-of-principle (Shanker et al. 2022, PMID 37100904, PMC10131520) validated this topology class as the primary productive scaffold for IgV-fold binders.

- Independent campaigns reporting high hit rates by BindCraft against IgV-containing surface targets (BCMA, CD19, CD22) consistently used lengths of 50-120 residues with helical-bundle scaffolds, and RFdiffusion literature shows that 80-100 residue 3-helix bundles are the modal output for compact globular binder design (PMID 40705894, PMC12313176; PMID 41415384, PMC12710756).

CONFIDENCE: med-high. The convergent evidence from (i) functional hotspot mapping, (ii) the only published de novo miniprotein campaign directly on TREM2 (Perera et al. 2026) confirming helical topology, and (iii) broad IgV-fold binder-design precedent all point in the same direction. Confidence is not "high" because no peer-reviewed co-crystal structure of a de novo binder with TREM2 yet exists, and the two validated TREM2 miniprotein hits (BindCraft8, Odesign2) have not had their atomic interfaces resolved.

WOULD-FALSIFY / OPEN QUESTIONS: (1) A high-resolution co-crystal showing a beta-hairpin or beta-sandwich scaffold dominating the hydrophobic patch would falsify the helical-bundle preference. (2) If RFdiffusion/BindCraft screens against TREM2 at lengths below 60 residues or above 100 residues achieve substantially higher ipTM scores and experimental validation rates than 60-100 residue helical bundles, the length claim would require revision. (3) If the basic-site epitope (R47/R76 region) rather than the hydrophobic-patch epitope (L69/W70) proves more druggable for miniproteins (e.g., via a negatively charged helix face), the hotspot specification would need correction.

Sources:

content.text:
I now have sufficient evidence across all three sub-questions. Here is the synthesised hypothesis.

---

HYPOTHESIS: The apical CDR-loop hydrophobic patch ("front face") of IgV-class targets is designable by RFdiffusion-based pipelines when that face presents a concave, aromatic-rich surface (e.g. Tyr/Phe/Trp residues within the CDR1/CDR2-equivalent loops), but default hotspot-directed RFdiffusion achieves very low in silico pass rates (~1%) on flat or polar IgV faces. For TREM2 specifically, the distal CDR-loop hydrophobic site — not the basic electropositive site — constitutes the druggable locus for this approach, and ipTM >= 0.70 (composite 0.8*ipTM + 0.2*pTM >= 0.70) is the empirically adopted AF2-multimer quality gate for declaring a design as a candidate in this fold class.

EVIDENCE:

- The canonical PD-1/PD-L1 interaction is mediated by GFCC' beta-strand strands of both IgV domains placing them perpendicular; hydrogen bonds, hydrophobic contacts, and pi-pi stacking across the CC'FG/GFCC' strands define this flat-face homodimerisation logic. Literature explicitly notes "no contribution from CDR-like loops, as opposed to CTLA-4/CD80." This establishes that the "front beta-sheet face" of IgV-class proteins is a documented protein-protein interaction surface, confirming the epitope is geometrically accessible and precedented for binder targeting. (PMCID PMC6067980, PMID 29848279; PMCID PMC4752817, PMID 26602187)

- For TREM2 specifically, the first crystal structure revealed two candidate binding surfaces: "a large hydrophobic site located on the distal end of the molecule in the CDR loops" and a basic electropositive site. The hydrophobic CDR-loop site, not the basic site, is where disease-associated variants (R47H, R62H) destabilise loop conformations and where lipid/apoE interactions occur, making it the structurally defined anchor for protein-level recognition. (PMCID PMC11721465, PMID 39789647; PMCID PMC12519512, PMID 41085188)

- De novo binder design on IgSF-fold targets using RFdiffusion (KIT, PDGFRalpha, FCRL5) achieves only ~0.98% in silico success when conditioned on hotspots alone, rising to 9.2% with beta-strand-interface conditioning. This directly quantifies the difficulty of flat IgV-class faces for default RFdiffusion and establishes that conditioning strategy is the primary determinant of yield. (PMCID PMC12852815, PMID 41519838)

- The original RFdiffusion benchmarking paper noted that "high-affinity binders can be identified from dozens of designs... at least for the non-polar sites targeted here; further studies will be required to assess success rates on more polar target sites." This explicitly flags polar, flat target faces as the hard regime. The TREM2 CDR-loop hydrophobic patch — which is non-polar and concave — therefore sits in the more tractable sub-regime relative to the basic site. (PMCID PMC10468394, PMID 37433327)

- Across published RFdiffusion + AF2-multimer binder design pipelines, the consensus in silico quality threshold used to call a design a true binder is ipTM >= 0.70, with the AF2-multimer composite score (0.8*ipTM + 0.2*pTM) used for ranking. Interface pAE < 10 and binder pLDDT > 85 are applied as co-filters. (PMCID PMC12952271, PMID 41289261; PMCID PMC12852815 filter: pAE < 10, pLDDT > 85, DeltaDeltaG < -30)

- The PD-L1 GFCC' face hydrophobic patch presents Tyr56, Tyr123, and a tightly packed aromatic cluster that serves as the primary pi-pi stacking anchor for PD-1 and for designed binders. Successful binders across IgV targets consistently exploit such aromatic clusters for shape complementarity; the loss of these contacts (as tested with tryptophan-to-Asp substitution in CDR loops in adjacent literature) abolishes binding. This supports a generalised IgV design rule: aromatic residues on the target face are the primary hotspot atoms, and designed binders must present complementary aromatic or hydrophobic residues. (PMCID PMC12703914, PMID 41332011; PMCID PMC4645341, PMID 26378169)

CONFIDENCE: med — The TREM2 CDR-loop hydrophobic face designation is supported by crystal structure data and biophysical evidence; the difficulty gradient (flat/polar < concave/hydrophobic) is directly quantified for IgSF-class targets in PMC12852815. However, no published RFdiffusion run directly on TREM2 IgV exists in the literature retrieved; the ipTM thresholds cited are from general binder pipelines, not TREM2-specific benchmarks.

WOULD-FALSIFY / OPEN QUESTIONS: (1) If a systematic RFdiffusion screen targeting the TREM2 CDR-loop hydrophobic patch fails to yield ipTM > 0.70 designs despite aromatic hotspot conditioning, the hypothesis that concavity and hydrophobicity predict tractability would be refuted. (2) If binders experimentally confirmed on the TREM2 basic (electropositive) site show higher affinity than those to the hydrophobic site, the designability prediction would require revision. (3) The TREM2 CDR-loop region contains flexible loops (L1/CDR1-equivalent near R47) whose dynamics may suppress AF2-multimer confidence independently of true binding energy — a high-ipTM design that fails SPR would indicate the AF2 filter mispredicts floppy IgV apical sites, which is the main falsifier for the quantitative scoring claim.

# BindCraft Sequence and Filtering Recommendations

Based on the documentation provided, here's what I found:

## (1) Sequence Composition Filters

The document does not specify recommended thresholds for charge, hydrophobic fraction, tryptophan content, or entropy. However, it mentions that **"ProteinMPNN to optimize the core and surface composition"** is applied and notes the use of **"soluble" MPNN weights** that produce **"a primarily negatively charged surface."**

## (2) AF2 ipTM or pAE Thresholds

No specific numerical thresholds are provided. The document states that **"i_pTM to be a good binary predictor of binding (i.e. binder or non-binder), however it is not predictive of affinity."** It identifies **"pLDDT, i_pTM and i_pAE AlphaFold2 filters to be most discriminative"** but does not quantify cutoff values.

## (3) Soluble Expression Rates or BLI Hit Rates

Neither metric is mentioned in this documentation. The text notes binders are **"usually well behaved biochemically, can be readily purified from E.coli"** and are **"highly thermostable,"** but provides no quantitative expression or binding data.

# RFdiffusion Protein Design: Key Experimental and Filtering Details

## (1) BLI/SPR Hit Rates

The study reports experimental success rates for protein binder design:
- **Overall binder success rate: 19%** across five targets (IL-7Rα, InsR, PD-L1, TrkA, HA), representing approximately "two orders of magnitude" improvement over previous Rosetta-based approaches
- Success defined as "binding at or above 50% of the maximal response for the positive control" at 10 μM concentration
- This contrasts sharply with earlier campaigns requiring "tens of thousands" of sequences tested

## (2) AF2 Filtering Thresholds

The paper specifies multiple AF2-based success criteria:

For binder design: "AF2 pLDDT of the monomer > 80, AF2 interaction pAE < 10, AF2 r.m.s.d. monomer vs design < 1 Å"

For general design validation: "mean predicted aligned error (pAE), less than five" and "globally within a 2 Å backbone root mean-squared deviation (r.m.s.d.) of the designed structure"

The document does not explicitly describe charge, hydrophobic fraction, tryptophan, or entropy-based sequence filters applied during design selection.

## (4) E. coli Soluble Expression Data

Key expression results:
- **Unconditional monomers**: "9/18 designs expressed, with a major peak at the expected elution volume"
- **TIM barrel designs**: "10/11 express and elute predominantly as monomers"
- **Symmetric oligomers**: "at least 87 had oligomerization states closely consistent" (608 tested)
- **Ni²⁺ binders**: "37/44 designs had SEC chromatograms consistent with the intended oligomeric state"

## (5) ProteinMPNN Variants

The study mentions "typically sampling eight sequences per design" but does not compare different ProteinMPNN variants or training approaches.

content.text:
I now have sufficient data to synthesize a well-grounded evidence-backed hypothesis. Let me compile the findings.

---

HYPOTHESIS: For de novo mini-protein binders (40-150 aa) generated by RFdiffusion/BindCraft + ProteinMPNN + AF2-multimer pipelines, the dominant bottleneck separating in silico-passing designs from BLI-detectable binders is binder surface hydrophobicity and net charge balance, not AF2 ipTM score per se; applying a surface hydrophobic exposure threshold of ≤35% and enforcing a negatively-biased net charge via MPNNsol (soluble-weight ProteinMPNN) constitutes the single sequence-composition intervention most predictive of soluble E. coli expression and BLI yield, and should be applied as a mandatory post-AF2 filter rather than an optional one.

---

EVIDENCE:

- The primary RFdiffusion binder design paper (Watson, Bennett, Baker et al., *Nature* 2023) reports an overall experimental binding success rate of approximately 19% across five targets (IL-7Ra, InsR, PD-L1, TrkA, HA) using the filter set pLDDT > 80, pAE_interaction < 10, monomer RMSD < 1 A; critically, no explicit sequence-level composition filters (charge, hydrophobic fraction, Trp count) were applied in the primary design pipeline, meaning structural confidence alone defined the shipped cohort. (PMID 37433327, PMC10468394)

- BindCraft, which integrates MPNNsol (ProteinMPNN retrained with solubility-promoting weights) alongside the standard interface-focused sequence design step, reports BLI experimental success rates of 10-100% across seven targets, with a mean of approximately 46% (PD-L1: 78%, PD-1: 24%, IFNAR2: 33%); the pipeline explicitly applies a binder surface hydrophobic exposure filter of < 35% as a mandatory post-hallucination filter, and uses MPNNsol to generate a primarily negatively-charged non-interface surface. (PMID 40866699, PMC12507698)

- Independently, the Baker/Gerben laboratory demonstrated that reducing surface hydrophobicity via redesign — filtering designs with > 35% exposed hydrophobic surface area — was directly causal in converting insoluble, aggregating constructs into soluble expressors in E. coli, confirming the mechanistic link between this threshold and expression outcome. (PMID 36627259, PMC9850923)

- A February 2025 preprint (Khakerwala et al., *bioRxiv* 10.1101/2025.02.07.636769) applying RFdiffusion to six eukaryotic targets (STAT3, FGF4, EGF, PDGF-BB, CD4, Strep-Tag II) with only AF2-based structural filters reports that binders for five of six targets failed due to low expression, nonspecific binding, or undetectable affinity in biochemical detection assays, explicitly attributing failures to insufficient sequence-level developability filtering upstream of experimental synthesis.

- The E. coli proteome literature establishes that amino acid composition, hydrophobicity, and net charge are the dominant predictors of inclusion body formation; supercharging (introduction of negatively-charged surface residues) has been validated to promote solubility in diverse expressed proteins, providing a mechanistic rationale for why MPNNsol's negatively-biased surface composition would confer expression benefit. (PMID 36033675, PMC9404520; PMID 27166796, PMC4864186)

- On the soluble_mpnn vs. vanilla ProteinMPNN question: no peer-reviewed head-to-head comparison with paired BLI outcomes exists as of June 2026. BindCraft documentation states MPNNsol is applied to all non-interface positions but provides no A/B quantitative comparison. The HER2 minibinder study (PMID 40502157, PMC12157515) using standard ProteinMPNN (FastRelax) achieved only ~6.5% experimental success rate from 31 designs with pAE < 10 / pLDDT > 70 filtering, consistent with the hypothesis that omitting solubility-aware sequence design depresses yield.

---

CONFIDENCE: med — The causal direction (MPNNsol + surface hydrophobicity filter -> improved BLI yield) is mechanistically coherent and consistent across BindCraft's multi-target dataset, but no controlled A/B trial directly randomizing MPNNsol vs vanilla MPNN with paired BLI readout has been published. The 46% BindCraft mean is confounded by target selection bias (many targets have native hotspot grooves favorable to helical binders) and BindCraft's use of higher AF2-based ipTM/ipAE thresholds alongside MPNNsol.

---

WOULD-FALSIFY / OPEN QUESTIONS:
- A controlled experiment expressing the same RFdiffusion backbone pool through vanilla ProteinMPNN vs MPNNsol, with BLI hit rate as the primary readout on the same target, would directly falsify or confirm the MPNNsol advantage claim.
- If systematic analysis of BLI failures showed that non-expressed designs have AF2 pAE scores statistically indistinguishable from expressors, that would suggest structure-confidence rather than sequence composition is the operative variable, falsifying (a).
- Whether a net charge constraint (e.g., at least -2 to -5 total charge at pH 7.4) adds discriminatory power beyond the 35% surface hydrophobicity filter alone remains an open quantitative question — no paper has reported the two independently in the same dataset.
- The tryptophan and sequence-entropy dimensions are genuinely uncharacterized in this lineage: published Baker-lineage papers do not impose Trp-count or Shannon-entropy filters, and no paper has retrospectively correlated these parameters with BLI outcome.

---

Sources:
- [De novo design of protein structure and function with RFdiffusion (Watson et al., Nature 2023) - PMC10468394](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10468394/)
- [BindCraft: one-shot design of functional protein binders (Pacesa et al.) - PMC12507698](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12507698/)
- [De Novo Design of High-Affinity HER2-Targeting Protein Minibinders - PMC12650588](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12650588/)
- [Design of Diverse Asymmetric Pockets — surface hydrophobicity filter - PMC9850923](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9850923/)
- [RFdiffusion low success rate preprint (Khakerwala et al., bioRxiv 2025)](https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/2025.02.07.636769v1)
- [BindCraft de novo binder design wiki (Martin Pacesa / GitHub)](https://github.com/martinpacesa/BindCraft/wiki/De-novo-binder-design-with-BindCraft)
- [Improved protein binder design using beta-pairing targeted RFdiffusion - Nature Communications](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-025-67866-3)
- [Supercharging for E. coli solubility (PMC4864186)](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4864186/)
- [Inclusion body formation determinants in E. coli (PMC9404520)](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9404520/)

# Run plan & reasoning — TREM2 IgSF binders

Target: human TREM2 V-type Ig-like ectodomain. User requires ipSAE ≥ 0.88.
Per learned skills the unconditioned-RFD3 ceiling here is ~0.82; 0.88 is
above the architecture's empirical ceiling. Spending the full 4-round
budget chasing it with structural pivots, but I will be honest about the
gap in the final report.

## Target resolution
- PDB 5ELI chain A; chain B also present (dimer in crystal).
- Full chain spans 20-201 with a 132-200 gap (stalk absent). Use crop **20-131** (112 aa IgSF domain).
- Sequence verified against the user-supplied 113-aa construct (His-tag end).
- Cropped target PDB written to /workspace/pdb_fetch_1/5ELI_chainA_20-131.pdb.

## Round-1 research scouts (§1.5, MANDATORY)
Three parallel scouts (`research` Sonnet tier, all returned without filter refusal):

1. **TREM2 binder precedent** — Perera 2026 (PMID 42079091) describes two
   experimentally-validated de novo TREM2 minibinders, **BindCraft8** and
   **Odesign2**, both helix-loop-helix wrapping the apical hydrophobic tip
   at L69/W70. Cyclic peptide TP4 (Shu 2025) also targets the same patch.
   IgV mini-binder precedent: 60-120 aa α-helical bundles dominate
   (Shanker 2022 PD-1/PD-L1, BindCraft IgV targets).
2. **IgV designability** — PMC12852815 quantifies: unconditioned RFD on
   IgSF targets = ~1% in-silico pass; β-strand conditioning lifts to 9.2%.
   Our wrapper has no strand conditioning lever. ipTM ≥ 0.70 + pAE < 10 +
   binder pLDDT > 85 = standard accept gate; ipSAE not benchmarked
   target-specifically.
3. **Mini-binder developability** — Bennett 2023 RFdiffusion: ~19% BLI hit
   rate across 5 targets; BindCraft adds MPNNsol + ≤35% surface
   hydrophobic exposure + negative net charge filter → 10-100% (mean ~46%).
   Vanilla MPNN at temp 0.1 ≠ MPNNsol; expect some shipped designs to
   need post-hoc surface review. No A/B trial exists.

## Due-diligence (§1.6)
- **Structural sandbox (biopython SASA + NeighborSearch on 5ELI):**
  W44 SASA=132, L69=65, W70=39, L71=143, F74=124, W78=68 — all exposed,
  all surface aromatic/hydrophobic. CDR1 (W44 cluster) and CDR2 (L69/W70/L71/F74/W78)
  both presentable; CDR3 (R98) is on the periphery.
- The scout's literature L69/W70 ≈ the learned skill's F74/W78. Both are
  pointing at the apical CDR2 hydrophobic patch — same surface, slightly
  different anchor pick.

## Debate (§1.7) — adjudicated
Contested point: which hotspot set for round 1?
- **Learned (3 prior TREM2 runs):** {A44, A74, A76, A78} — proven ipSAE ~0.82,
  α-helical bundle, W78 chronically unsatisfied at 75% sat.
- **Scout (Perera/Bhatt):** L69/W70 are the published functional hotspots;
  ApoE/TDP-43 binders engage L69/W70 anchor.
- **Resolution:** HEDGE. Both sets target the same apical face. Run both
  branches in round 1; the data adjudicates. Length 75-95 covers both
  helical-bundle (75-85) and slightly-longer extended-loop (90-95).
- **Adjudicated design hypothesis (round 1):**
  - Branch A (proven CDR2-ridge): {A44, A74, A76, A78}, len 75-90, 6 designs
  - Branch B (literature L69/W70 anchor): {A69, A70, A74, A78}, len 75-95, 6 designs
  - MPNN n=3 each, temp=0.1; ESM ≥70; AF2 colabfold num_models=1.
  - Target: at least one design at ipSAE ≥ 0.78 in either branch, then partial-t polish in round 2.

Budget check: round 1 of 4. Will use all 4 unless gate met (≥3 designs at
ipSAE≥0.88 AND ipTM≥0.7 AND complex pLDDT > 93 AND hotspot sat ≥0.70 AND BSA ≳700).

1	# Tool skill: `design.rfdiffusion3` — backbone generation
2	
3	Read this before pipeline **step 4** (backbone generation). It is the
4	operational detail for the one-line summary in the core skill.
5	
6	`mcp__proteinclaw_tools__design_rfdiffusion3`:
7	- `target_pdb`, `target_chain`, `hotspot_residues` (from step 3)
8	- `binder_length`: range e.g. `"60-80"`
9	- `num_designs`: **you decide — see "Sizing the funnel" below**. The
10	  YAML default of 4 is a smoke-test value, not a guideline. Range
11	  1–32; agent must reason about target difficulty and round budget
12	  rather than copy the default.
13	- `num_timesteps=50` default — well-tested, don't raise.
14	- `step_scale=3`, `gamma_0=0.2`, `is_non_loopy=true` are the
15	  RFD3 PPI tutorial canon. Don't touch unless the user asks for
16	  diversity over designability.
17	
18	## Partial diffusion — round-2 refinement of a proven backbone
19	
20	Two **mutually exclusive** ways to call this tool:
21	- **De-novo (cold start):** `target_pdb` + `hotspot_residues` + `binder_length`
22	  (the params above). Use in round 1.
23	- **Partial diffusion (refine a winner):** `start_pdb` + `partial_t`. Use in
24	  round 2+ once you have a docking backbone worth polishing — it's the
25	  highest-impact refinement (5–10× hit-rate on hard targets).
26	
27	Partial-diffusion params:
28	- `start_pdb`: path under `/workspace` to a prior **binder+target complex**
29	  PDB — the best AF2 winner from a previous round (chain A = binder,
30	  chain B = target by our convention).
31	- `partial_t`: **Angstroms of noise** to add before re-denoising (RFD3 caps
32	  at 15). **2–6 Å = polish** (stay near the winner), **8–12 Å = explore**.
33	  It is NOT a timestep count — small means closer to the input.
34	- `binder_chain` / `target_chain`: chain letters in `start_pdb` (default
35	  `A` / `B`). `num_designs`, `num_timesteps`, `step_scale`, `gamma_0`,
36	  `is_non_loopy` still apply.
37	- **Do NOT pass `binder_length` or `hotspot_residues`** in this mode — the
38	  geometry comes from `start_pdb`; RFD3 rejects a length arg with partial_t.
39	
40	RFD3 re-noises the *whole* complex by `partial_t` Å (target included), so for
41	small `partial_t` the target barely moves; downstream MPNN→ESM→AF2 re-design
42	and re-score against the clean target sequence anyway. Output is the usual set
43	of backbone PDBs (binder chain A, target chain B) — feed them to ProteinMPNN
44	exactly like de-novo outputs.
45	
46	## Sizing the funnel — how to pick `num_designs` (and downstream `num_sequences`)
47	
48	There is no single right number. **You are expected to choose it
49	based on signals available before the run starts.** Reason from these
50	inputs and state your choice (with one-line justification) in your
51	narration before the RFD3 call:
52	
53	1. **Target difficulty signal** (highest weight)
54	   - Co-crystal binder available, well-modeled hotspot face, no gaps
55	     in the crop → **easy**: 4–6 backbones is enough to validate the
56	     pipeline; ramp later if round-1 yields zero hits.
57	   - Hotspots inferred (no known binder), surface-level epitope, or
58	     intrinsically-disordered region nearby → **hard**: start at
59	     **8–12 backbones**, expect to need round 2.
60	   - Novel target class (GPCR, membrane protein, glycosylated site,
61	     PDB resolution > 3.0 Å) → **very hard**: 12–16 backbones
62	     minimum, and warn the user that hit-rate may be low.
63	
64	2. **Round budget** (`--rounds N`, surfaced in the per-run addendum)
65	   - `rounds=1`: spend more here — there's no second chance. Bias
66	     toward the upper end of your difficulty band.
67	   - `rounds=2+`: smaller round 1 is fine because round 2 will use
68	     partial-diffusion on round-1 winners (5–10× hit-rate boost,
69	     core skill "Self-refining loop"). Round 2 typically needs only
70	     4–8 refined designs.
71	
72	3. **Compute envelope** (sanity check, not a primary input)
73	   - Each backbone is 1–3 min RFD3 + 30 s MPNN/seq + 24 s ESM (batched)
74	     + 5–15 min AF2/sequence. **A single A100 finishes ~6–8 candidates
75	     through AF2 per hour.** If you plan 12 backbones × 8 sequences =
76	     96 AF2 jobs, that's ~12–24 h of wall-time. Don't quietly schedule
77	     that without flagging it in your narration.
78	   - The Bennett 2023 gold standard used ~10,000 backbones per target.
79	     We're operating 2–3 orders of magnitude below that — be honest in
80	     your summary about exploratory vs exhaustive scale.
81	
82	4. **Stopping criterion as feedback**: the core skill "Self-refining
83	   loop" defines success as ≥5 designs with `complex_confidence > 75`.
84	   If round 1 finishes with that already met, do not run round 2.
85	   If round 1 finishes with zero such designs, round 2 must increase
86	   `num_designs` *and* shift to partial-diffusion — repeating the same
87	   numbers will not help.
88	
89	**Anti-pattern:** picking `num_designs=2` because the YAML default is
90	4 and "less is faster." If the agent can't justify the number from the
91	four inputs above, default to **8** (the figure most pipelines —
92	BindCraft, ProteinDJ, dl_binder_design — converge on for a real round).
93	
94	**Critical:** read the envelope's `output_binder_chain` and
95	`output_target_chain`. RFD3 assigns chain IDs by contig order
96	(typically binder = A, target = B), but the wrapper detects it
97	empirically — never assume a letter.
98	
99	**If RFD3 fails with "Residue X not found in atom array":** the crop
100	spans an unmodeled residue. Pick a different crop range from step 1b's
101	gap list, OR a different PDB.
